traits.carpels.note: Gibson and Nobel, The Cactus Primer (1986) pp. 23 to 25, Stenocereus thurberi: 11 to 12 stigma lobes on a white style slightly exserted through the stamens; the carpels are as many as the lobes.

traits.stamens.note: Gibson and Nobel, The Cactus Primer (1986) pp. 23 to 25, Stenocereus thurberi: hundreds of white stamens, all about 2 cm long, the upper ones exserted evenly like a shaving brush.

traits.stem_colour.note: Anderson, The Cactus Family (2001) p. 649, Stenocereus thurberi: stems green; dark green, as Anderson's photograph shows them.

traits.spine_colour.note: Anderson, The Cactus Family (2001) p. 649, Stenocereus thurberi: radial spines greyish, to 1 cm.

traits.central_spine_colour.note: Anderson, The Cactus Family (2001) p. 649, Stenocereus thurberi: central spines greyish to blackish.

traits.areole_wool_colour.note: Gibson and Nobel, The Cactus Primer (1986) p. 14: the areoles' hairs red at first, turning black.

traits.corolla_shape.note: Anderson, The Cactus Family (2001) p. 649, Stenocereus thurberi: flowers funnelform, white, 4 to 8 cm long; fruit red. Gibson and Nobel, The Cactus Primer pp. 22 to 25: flowers whitish to pinkish, 6 to 8 cm, with 25 or more perianth parts (as the family's default). Neither gives the flower's width or the fruit's size, so those stay set by hand.

traits.fruit_colour_ripe.note: Anderson, The Cactus Family (2001) p. 649, Stenocereus thurberi: flowers funnelform, white, 4 to 8 cm long; fruit red. Gibson and Nobel, The Cactus Primer pp. 22 to 25: flowers whitish to pinkish, 6 to 8 cm, with 25 or more perianth parts (as the family's default). traits.height_max_m.note: Britton and Rose vol. 2 (1920), as Lemaireocereus thurberi: usually trunkless, with 5 to 20 or more erect stems 3 m to 7 m tall.

traits.wood_density_basic_kg_m3.note: GWDD v.2.2 species aggregate for Stenocereus thurberi (gwddagg_v2.2_species.csv, read): specific gravity 0.49 (wsg_est, the database's hierarchical-model species mean, from 1 record in 1 source); trunks 0.49, branches 0.49. Basic density (oven-dry mass over green volume) is the specific gravity times 1000 kg/m3.

traits.flower_zone.note: Gibson and Nobel, The Cactus Primer (1986) p. 22, organ pipe cactus: showy sessile flowers, each from a single areole, near the apex and along the sides of the branches.

traits.note: Britton and Rose's The Cactaceae (vol. 2, 1920, p. 97), as Lemaireocereus thurberi: stems 15 to 20 cm thick, with 12 to 17 low, rounded ribs; areoles 1 to 1.5 cm apart, rarely 3 cm, large and brown-felted. The spines are not told apart as radials and centrals.

generator.params.note: Hand-set from general knowledge of the species: a clump of a dozen or more ribbed columns, 15 to 20 cm thick, that rise from a short base, spread out and curve up into a vase 3 to 7 m tall; new stems come from the base over decades. Pale flowers open near the stem tips, followed by red, spiny fruit. Not fitted to measurements.

allometry.note: Rough stem heights from general knowledge: a few metres by 70 years, about 5 m by 120. Wide tolerances.

appearance.note: Colours chosen by eye from photographs: dark green stems with 12 to 19 ribs, areoles 2 cm apart with dark felt, short dark radial spines and one to three longer centrals that grey with age; creamy white to lavender flowers. Its flower, bud and fruit are drawn from its characters by the rules at Cactaceae and the flowering plants: tepals on a spiral, as many and as broad as the family's rules give, on a floral cup above the inferior ovary, its stamens, style and stigma lobes, and its fruit from its stated colour, size and surface. Until 2026-10-18 its flower and fruit looks were partly set by hand (round tepal tips, a centre and an accent colour by eye), and a look set by hand keeps the rule that gives it the year its months state from running, so it flowered and fruited all year.

taxon.note: Scientific and common names (and USDA symbol, where given) as the spec's authors wrote them, and the genus the scientific name is written in.

growth_form.note: The growth form the spec's authors chose from the plant's habit.

growth.note: The growth plan (years, step, keyframes) chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

variants.note: The environments, conditions and seeds chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

traits.limb_angle.note: Flora of North America vol. 4 (read on eFloras 2026-10-19), Stenocereus thurberi: shrubs, branching basal, 3-6[-12+] m; stems erect; the genus: trees or shrubs, erect, arching, or procumbent, mostly branched from base. Its stems are its limbs, erect from its base, so the family's rule fans them out to a vase of columns that hold their angle. Until round 5 they leaned out by hand 25 degrees and turned upright within a metre (bend 0.35), a bundle narrowing upward against photographs of a vase.

traits.flowering_months.note: Flora of North America vol. 4 (read on eFloras 2026-10-20), Stenocereus thurberi: 'Flowering (Mar)Apr-Jul[-Dec]; fruiting mostly Jul-Aug.' The usual months kept, the bracketed range outside the flora area left out. Until 2026-10-20 a model estimate of May to July and July to September.

traits.anther_colour.note: Gibson and Nobel, The Cactus Primer (1986) pp. 23 to 25, Stenocereus thurberi: stamens in hundreds, white, all about 2 cm long, the upper ones exserted evenly like a shaving brush.

traits.filament_colour.note: Gibson and Nobel, The Cactus Primer (1986) pp. 23 to 25, Stenocereus thurberi: stamens white; style white, slightly exserted through the stamen mass.

traits.fruit_shape.note: Flora of North America vol. 4 (read on eFloras 2026-10-18), Stenocereus: fruits spheric; the Cactus Primer (pp. 23 to 25) draws the organ pipe's globose, densely spiny fruit.
